pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: lib/agent/reviewerEnv.ts:39 The per-engine environment is decided inside the argv builder, so reviewerEnv has to build a fake reviewer call (model "m", cwd ".", empty prompt) to read the env field back out; the env decision sits in the wrong module and its caller works around it.

techniques.evidence: lib/agent/reviewerEnv.ts:39 The standard calls this depth in the wrong place: the caller reaches past the module with made-up inputs to get one decision out. Every engine's env is {} today, so nothing breaks yet, but any engine whose env depends on its call would be computed from fake values.
lib/agent/agentArgs.ts:62 The binary is a real substitution point: ARTICLES_AGENT_BIN swaps in the stub agent, and env is a parameter, not a global read.
lib/agent/reviewerCommand.ts:13 Each engine's fence is a pure function a probe can assert without spawning anything. Spawning is kept in spawnTurn.ts.
lib/agent/cliSeam.ts:9 The reasoning door and the agent door are separate seams, not one function with a mode flag, and the one rule they share is imported once so it cannot drift.

pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/board/_port/port.ts:35 The Board port's switch is a hardcoded constant, so the 374-line fixture adapter (fixture.ts) is never reached by any route, test or kit specimen (grep finds only port.ts importing fixtureBoard). It is a seam nobody substitutes at, carrying a hand-written copy of the kernel's decision rules.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/board/_port/port.ts:35 The standard says a seam nobody substitutes at is already the failure, and a double must be checked against the same contract; the fixture side has no callers and no contract suite. The real side's Deps injection (real.ts:63, used by tests/next-server/board-real.test.ts) is the seam that is actually used.

app/(studio)/board/_port/fixture.ts:5 The kernel's decision rules (stale base, undo inverse, the blind EXISTS guard, commit refusal, the token) are written a second time in a file nothing runs, so one decision is encoded in two places and the copy can drift without anyone noticing.
